newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends lower, gilts up in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends lower, gilts up in light trade.

text.p: Indian call money rates ended Monday at 4.75-5.25 percent down from opening quotes of 5.75-6.50 percent on ample liquidity, dealers said.
Most of the day's trade was in a 5.50-5.75 percent band, with stray deals at lower levels, they said.
Many dealers said they expect call money to trade in a 5.0-5.5 percent band on Tuesday but some said a late afternoon announcement of a bond auction will push rates higher.
The government announced a 30-billion-rupee auction of eight-year bonds for August 11.
"I think call money may move up to around 7.0-8.0 percent by weekend," said a foreign bank dealer.
Prices of government securities were up in light trade, dealers said. They said volumes were light as traders seemed to be more comfortable with call money levels below 5.0 percent.
The 11.83 percent government stock 2003 rose to 103.05 rupees from its previous close of 102.95 rupees while the 12.59 percent 2004 stock improved 106.00 rupees from 105.92 rupees.
Dealers said zero coupon bonds were in demand with the zero-coupon 2000 moving up to 74.70 rupees from its previous close of 74.45 rupees.
The yield on treasury bills maturing in April 1998 fell to 7.75 percent from its previous close of 7.80 percent, dealers said.
